page: Microsoft Azure L128ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64), this instance provisions 128 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1024 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 23038 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, designed to accommodate large dataset footprints requiring direct-attached, low-latency disk access. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

The combination of ARM-based CPU execution with high memory density offers qualitative resource efficiency compared to traditional x86 storage instances, providing compute and storage consolidation within a single node. However, adopting the arm64 architecture necessitates that software stacks, runtimes, and operating system packages have native ARM compatibility. Additionally, the integrated 23038 GB NVMe disk provides direct-attached storage; while suitable for high-throughput operations, data persistence architectures must account for the local nature of the disks or utilize supported Premium Storage capabilities.

With its extensive local disk capacity and large 1024 GB memory allocation, the L128ps_v5 is configured for heavy I/O operations and data-intensive pipelines. Appropriate deployments include distributed NoSQL databases, large relational database engines, high-volume transactional processing, search indexing clusters, and data warehousing systems that benefit from low-latency local storage access.
description: Microsoft Azure L128ps_v5 is an arm64 storage-optimized virtual machine delivered via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates 128 dedicated vCPUs, 1024 GB of memory with an 8 GB per core ratio, and 23038 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking discrete graphics processing hardware, the architecture focuses on compute density and I/O throughput. The ARM-based infrastructure delivers substantial processing and memory capacity for large-scale operations while maintaining hardware efficiency. Because the local NVMe storage provides low-latency direct throughput, workloads requiring remote persistence can also utilize supported Premium Storage configurations. The L128ps_v5 is configured for high-throughput data systems, including large-scale NoSQL and relational database management engines, real-time analytics platforms, distributed file systems, search indexing, and data warehousing workloads.
